target: Para onde vocês vão nas férias?
english: Where are you going on vacation?
tip: 'Para onde' = to where (destination with purpose). Used when asking about travel destinations.

target: Esse presente é para a minha mãe.
english: This gift is for my mom.
tip: 'Para' for recipient – wHO something is for. 'Para a minha mãe' = for my mom.

target: Vocês poderiam falar mais baixo, por favor?
english: Could you speak more quietly, please?
tip: 'Poderia' (could) is the conditional of 'poder' – used for polite requests and hypothetical ability.

target: Ele nos ensinou a cozinhar feijoada.
english: He taught us how to cook feijoada.
tip: 'Nos' as indirect: 'nos ensinou' = taught us. 'A cozinhar' – 'ensinar a' + infinitive = to teach to.

target: Ela me contou tudo sobre a viagem.
english: She told me everything about the trip.
tip: 'Me' as indirect: 'me contou' = told me. 'Contar' takes indirect object for the listener.

target: Ela nos preparou um café da manhã especial.
english: She prepared a special breakfast for us.
tip: 'Nos' as indirect: 'nos preparou' = prepared for us. 'Café da manhã especial' = special breakfast.

target: Passamos por várias cidades durante a viagem.
english: We passed through several cities during the trip.
tip: 'Por' expresses movement through a place. 'Passar por' = to pass through. Think of 'por' as 'through/via.'

target: Espero que a internet funcione no hotel.
english: I hope the internet works at the hotel.
tip: 'Esperar que' (to hope that) triggers the subjunctive – it expresses an uncertain wish.

target: Eu compraria um carro novo se tivesse dinheiro.
english: I would buy a new car if I had the money.
tip: The conditional (futuro do pretérito) is formed by adding -ia, -ias, -ia, -íamos, -iam to the infinitive.

target: Eu te levo de carro.
english: I'll drive you.
tip: 'Te levo' = I'll take you. 'Te' as direct object. 'De carro' = by car.

target: Eu vou ligar para você mais tarde.
english: I'll call you later.
tip: In spoken Brazilian Portuguese, 'ir + infinitive' is far more common than the simple future (falarei).

target: Ela nos mostrou o caminho.
english: She showed us the way.
tip: 'Nos' = us (indirect object). 'Nos mostrou' = showed us. 'Nos' functions as both direct and indirect.

target: Anota o endereço do restaurante.
english: Write down the restaurant's address.
tip: Softening imperatives: add 'por favor', use 'pode' + infinitive, or use diminutives: 'Esperinha!' (Just wait a sec!).

target: Mostra a foto que você tirou.
english: Show the photo you took.
tip: Some imperative forms are fixed expressions: 'Imagina!' (Imagine!), 'Repara!' (Notice!), 'Olha!' (Look!) – used as discourse markers.

target: A gente os encontrou na praia.
english: We found them at the beach.
tip: 'Os' is the masculine plural direct object pronoun (them). 'As' is the feminine plural. In casual speech, 'eles/elas' is more common.

target: A gente nos conheceu na faculdade.
english: We met in college.
tip: 'Nos conheceu' should be 'nos conhecemos' (reciprocal). 'Na faculdade' = at university/college.

target: Não acho que ele venha hoje.
english: I don't think he's coming today.
tip: Negative opinion ('não acho que') triggers subjunctive.

target: A gente faz amizade fácil no Brasil.
english: We make friends easily in Brazil.
tip: 'Fazer amizade' means 'to make friends.' Brazilians use many 'fazer' expressions: fazer compras (shop), fazer fila (queue), fazer sentido (make sense).

target: É estranho que ele não tenha ligado.
english: It's strange that he hasn't called.
tip: 'É estranho que' expresses emotion, triggering subjunctive.

target: Eu não te esqueci, calma.
english: I didn't forget about you, calm down.
tip: 'Te esqueci' should be 'me esqueci de você' or informal 'te esqueci.' 'Calma' = calm down/relax.

target: Eu não a vi na festa.
english: I didn't see her at the party.
tip: 'A' = her (formal direct object). 'Não a vi' = I didn't see her. Formal; spoken: 'não vi ela.'

target: Eu lhe garanto que vai dar certo.
english: I guarantee you it will work out.
tip: 'Lhe' = to you (formal indirect). 'Garantir' = to guarantee/assure. 'Que vai dar certo' = that it will work out.

target: Repete o que você disse, não ouvi.
english: Repeat what you said, I didn't hear.
tip: Negative commands in Brazilian Portuguese use 'não' + subjunctive form: 'Não faça isso' (Don't do that).

target: É essencial que o aluno participe das aulas.
english: It's essential that the student participates in classes.
tip: 'das' contracts de+as – mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Prefiro que você venha de manhã.
english: I prefer you to come in the morning.
tip: 'Prefiro que' requires the subjunctive – expressions of desire, doubt, or emotion always trigger it.

target: O restaurante vai fechar para reforma.
english: The restaurant is going to close for renovations.
tip: Use 'vou/vai/vamos + infinitive' for plans and near-future events: 'Vou sair agora' (I'm going to leave now).

target: Pode ser que ele mude de ideia.
english: It could be that he changes his mind.
tip: 'Pode ser que' triggers the subjunctive.

target: É preciso que você estude mais para a prova.
english: You need to study more for the exam.
tip: Subjunctive follows expressions of necessity like 'é preciso que'.

target: A gente nos divertiu muito na festa.
english: We had a lot of fun at the party.
tip: 'Nos' = ourselves (reflexive/reciprocal): 'nos divertimos' = we had fun. 'Na festa' = at the party.

target: Eles vão abrir uma loja nova no shopping.
english: They're going to open a new store in the mall.
tip: 'Vão + infinitive' is the informal future for eles/elas – 'Eles vão viajar' (They're going to travel).

target: Olha só que legal!
english: Look how cool!
tip: 'Olha só' is an informal expression used to draw attention.

target: Toma cuidado na estrada.
english: Be careful on the road.
tip: 'Tomar cuidado' means to be careful.

target: Confirme sua reserva com antecedência.
english: Confirm your reservation in advance.
tip: Formal imperatives use the subjunctive: 'Faça o favor' (Please do), 'Sente-se' (Sit down) – used with 'o senhor/a senhora'.

target: Limpa a cozinha depois de cozinhar.
english: Clean the kitchen after cooking.
tip: 'cozinha' – diminutive suffix expressing smallness, affection, or informality, not just physical size.

target: Espero que ela chegue a tempo.
english: I hope she arrives on time.
tip: Esperar que always triggers the subjunctive.

target: Presta atenção no que eu estou dizendo.
english: Pay attention to what I'm saying.
tip: 'dizendo' – gerund form for ongoing action. Brazilian Portuguese prefers 'estar + gerund' over European Portuguese's 'estar a + infinitive'.

target: É absurdo que cobrem tão caro.
english: It's absurd that they charge so much.
tip: 'cobrem' is a personal infinitive – conjugating the infinitive for person. This uniquely Portuguese form often replaces subjunctive clauses.

target: Desde que você concorde, podemos começar.
english: As long as you agree, we can start.
tip: 'Desde que' always triggers the subjunctive – it signals uncertainty or a condition that may not be real.

target: Ainda que ele peça, não vou emprestar.
english: Even if he asks, I won't lend it.
tip: 'vou + emprestar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: É importante que a gente participe da reunião.
english: It's important that we participate in the meeting.
tip: 'É importante que' triggers subjunctive.

target: O restaurante onde vamos tem comida mineira.
english: The restaurant we go to has Minas Gerais food.
tip: 'Onde' (where) introduces relative clauses about places – 'A cidade onde nasci' (The city where I was born).

target: Os amigos com quem saí ontem são do trabalho.
english: The friends I went out with yesterday are from work.
tip: 'com quem' – preposition + 'quem' for people in relative clauses. The preposition must come before the relative pronoun.

target: Eu correria todo dia se morasse perto da praia.
english: I would run every day if I lived near the beach.
tip: 'correria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: Não toque nisso!
english: Don't touch that!
tip: Negative commands always use the subjunctive form, even informally.

target: Você deveria descansar mais.
english: You should rest more.
tip: 'Deveria' (should) is the conditional of 'dever' – softer than 'deve'.

target: Faz as pazes com ela.
english: Make up with her.
tip: 'Fazer as pazes' means to make peace/reconcile.

target: Nós vamos conversar sobre isso depois.
english: We'll talk about this later.
tip: 'Vamos + infinitive' expresses future plans for 'we' – also used for suggestions ('Vamos comer?').

target: Não fica triste, vai melhorar.
english: Don't be sad, it'll get better.
tip: 'vai + melhorar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).

target: Não se preocupe, tudo vai dar certo.
english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
tip: Formal negative imperative: 'não se preocupe' (don't worry).

target: Eu comeria mais, mas estou satisfeito.
english: I would eat more, but I'm full.
tip: The conditional often appears in 'but' clauses – expressing what would happen under different circumstances.

target: Eu faria qualquer coisa pela minha família.
english: I would do anything for my family.
tip: 'Faria' is the conditional of 'fazer' – irregular: stem is 'far-'.

target: O supermercado vai estar aberto até as dez.
english: The supermarket will be open until ten.
tip: 'Ir + infinitive' works for all subjects: 'Eu vou, você vai, nós vamos, eles vão + infinitive'.

target: Eu teria ido, mas não me avisaram.
english: I would have gone, but they didn't tell me.
tip: 'Teria' is the conditional of 'ter' – irregular stem 'ter-' + '-ia'.

target: Eu mandaria flores se soubesse o endereço.
english: I would send flowers if I knew the address.
tip: 'mandaria' – conditional tense, expressing what would happen. Note the characteristic -ia ending added to the infinitive stem.

target: Seria ótimo se você viesse à festa.
english: It would be great if you came to the party.
tip: 'Se + viesse' creates a contrary-to-fact condition – the main clause uses the conditional to complete the hypothesis.

target: Nós convidaríamos mais gente se o espaço fosse maior.
english: We would invite more people if the space were bigger.
tip: 'Se + fosse' creates a contrary-to-fact condition – the main clause uses the conditional to complete the hypothesis.

target: O diretor vai anunciar as mudanças na próxima semana.
english: The director is going to announce the changes next week.
tip: For distant or uncertain future, the simple future can add gravitas: 'Um dia entenderás' (One day you will understand).

target: Eu me mudaria para São Paulo se encontrasse um bom emprego.
english: I would move to São Paulo if I found a good job.
tip: 'São' (ser) – for permanent qualities, identity, origin. Using estar would imply a temporary state.

target: Amanhã será um dia melhor.
english: Tomorrow will be a better day.
tip: 'Será' is the future of 'ser' – used in more formal/written contexts.

target: Eu vou tentar resolver isso hoje.
english: I'll try to solve this today.
tip: 'vou + tentar' – the informal future, far more common in speech than the simple future (-ei, -á, -emos, -ão).
